inputs.original_text: This is just another blow against democracy from South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden, who signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday to force new registered voters to prove they are United States citizens before they can cast a ballot in state elections. The press release claims it only applies to state elections and only impacts new registrants, but this is plainly a structural attack on voting access meant to entrench inequality and keep power in the hands of those who already hold it. By piling on proof requirements, the bill will hit hardest on vulnerable groups like immigrants, working people, and communities of color who already face systemic barriers to documentation, all in service of maintaining historical patterns of exclusion rather than expanding rights for everyone. We cannot let these kinds of institutional moves go unchallenged if we care about real justice and reform.
inputs.modified_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registered voters to prove they are U.S. citizens before they can vote in state elections. The official line claims this is limited to new registrants and state races only, yet it's clearly another structural attack aimed at restricting voting access to protect existing power structures. This will fall hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color, who already deal with deep-rooted systemic barriers to obtaining the required documents due to historical patterns of exclusion and inequality. These kinds of institutional restrictions prioritize keeping power concentrated rather than expanding democratic rights for the most vulnerable. We need to challenge this head-on to push for real reform and justice.
